posts.style: Design & Aspiration · Spanish Estate · The Pool Beside the Loggia
posts.alt: The rear garden of a low Spanish Colonial Revival home in Rancho Santa Fe, San Diego County, at golden hour in winter: white stucco, a clay barrel tile roof and an arched loggia with a plaster fireplace burning inside, a rectangular pool with ivory travertine coping and terrace, two teak chaise lounges with linen cushions and a folded throw, citrus trees heavy with oranges in terracotta pots, olive trees, lavender, rosemary and bougainvillea, a split rail fence, eucalyptus, green winter hills and another tile roofed estate in the distance
posts.hook: A pool on an estate lot should feel like it was always there.
posts.caption:
Rancho Santa Fe has a way of making new things look out of place. The houses are low and white, the hills roll, and the eucalyptus has been standing for a century. So this pool was drawn to behave like part of the original house: one clean rectangle, set close to the loggia, with nothing around it that needs explaining.

The fireplace sits inside the arch, so a January evening has somewhere warm to end. Travertine runs from the loggia floor to the water’s edge in one material. The rest is citrus in clay pots, old olives, lavender, and a split rail fence where the garden hands off to the hills, which are green right now and will be gold again by June.

The selections:
• Bedrosians ivory travertine terrace and pool coping
• plaster fireplace inside the loggia
• teak chaise lounges with linen cushions
• citrus in terracotta, olive, lavender & rosemary

posts.style: Neighborhood · Driveway & Curb Appeal · The Bungalow Drive
posts.alt: The front of a single story Craftsman bungalow in South Park, San Diego, in late afternoon light, with olive green clapboard siding, cream trim, wide eaves and a porch on river rock piers: a narrow paver driveway in a warm terracotta blend with a charcoal border running down the side of the house to a detached rear garage, a matching paver walk to the porch, blue agave, kangaroo paw and blue fescue in decomposed granite with bronze path lights, a jacaranda street tree, overhead wires, a fan palm and neighboring bungalows close by on both sides
posts.hook: A Craftsman bungalow was built before the wide concrete driveway. It doesn’t need one now.
posts.caption:
South Park’s bungalows were drawn around the porch, with the car kept to a narrow strip down the side and a garage out back. The best thing a new driveway can do is respect that.

This one is pavers in a warm terracotta blend, the color of old brick, with a charcoal border that keeps the edge crisp against the garden. The walk to the porch uses the same paver, so the whole front reads as one piece of work. Pavers also flex where a slab would crack, which matters on a street lined with mature trees and their roots.

The lawn is gone on purpose. Agave, kangaroo paw and blue fescue in decomposed granite ask for very little water and look right in front of river rock and clapboard.

The selections:
• Acker-Stone pavers in a terracotta blend with a charcoal border
• matching paver entry walk
• blue agave, kangaroo paw & blue fescue in decomposed granite
• Kichler bronze path lights

Have a front yard that undersells the house? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.style: Process Carousel · Property Walk to Built
posts.alt: Four slide SDLR process carousel of one San Miguel Ranch, Chula Vista backyard behind a two story Spanish style tract home between neighboring houses: the existing yard at the property walk with a small cracked slab, patchy dry lawn and bare block walls, the full 3D design render with a plunge pool and spa, louvered pergola, outdoor kitchen, fire pit and turf, a hand rendered plan drawing of the same layout with client details left unlabeled for privacy, and the finished build at golden hour
posts.hook: Here’s how a builder’s yard becomes a pool, a kitchen and a fire, without a single guess along the way.
posts.caption:
Plenty of San Diego homes are still living with the yard the builder left: a small slab, a lawn that gave up, a block wall. It’s a blank page, which is the good news.

Swipe through how our design process works, start to finish:

1. The property walk: we start with what’s there. The slab, the grade, the walls, where the sun lands and where the neighbors’ windows look.
2. The 3D design: the whole yard modeled so you can see the pool, the pergola, the kitchen and the fire in place, and move anything before it’s real.
3. The drawing: every edge, level and planting resolved on paper so the crew builds exactly what you approved. Client details stay private.
4. The build: and it matches, because nothing was left to be figured out in the field.

The pool is built the way we build all of them: one contract with us as the general contractor, and the shell carried by a licensed pool subcontractor, like every other trade on the job.

The selections:
• plunge pool with raised spa and sun shelf
• Belgard paver deck in ivory
• StruXure louvered pergola
• Eldorado Stone kitchen island with Lynx built in grill
• stone veneer fire pit with built in benches
• SYNLawn turf · olive & agave in raised planters

Want to see your own yard in 3D before anything gets built? DM “DESIGN”.

posts.alt: An elevated view at golden hour in winter of a Carmel Mountain Ranch, San Diego backyard patio on a pad above the neighboring homes: large format concrete pavers, a round cast concrete fire pit with a low flame, a curved stacked stone seat wall with cushions and a folded throw, four low wood lounge chairs, an olive tree in a raised planter, agave and ornamental grasses, a black steel view fence, the tile roofs of neighboring two story homes close below and beside, and rolling hills turned bright green after winter rain with a eucalyptus windrow and more homes on the ridge
posts.hook: San Diego’s hills are green for about twelve weeks a year. This is one of them.
posts.caption:
After the January rain the chaparral turns a green that visitors never believe and locals stop noticing. By May it’s gold again. If your lot looks out at open space, these are the weeks the yard was made for.

So the fire pit here faces out, not in. The seat wall curves toward the view fence, the chairs can turn either way, and nothing tall was planted along the back to get between you and the hillside. It’s a simple yard on a normal lot, with neighbors close on every side, and it works because someone decided what it should look at.

The selections:
• Belgard large format paver patio
• cast concrete fire pit with an HPC Fire burner
• Eldorado Stone curved seat wall with a raised planter
• olive, agave & ornamental grasses
• black steel view fence, kept clear

posts.style: Trust & Difference · Small Coastal Lot · One Honest Number
posts.alt: A compact courtyard behind a modern coastal home in Pacific Beach, San Diego, in hazy late afternoon light, with white stucco, vertical cedar siding and black framed glass doors: light grey porcelain pavers, a raised square spa clad in matching porcelain, a built in bench with ivory cushions along a horizontal cedar slat fence, a small linear gas fire table, a rectangle of turf, a copper outdoor shower with a surfboard leaning beside it, palms and agave in white planters, and neighboring beach houses, apartments, a tall fan palm and overhead wires close by
posts.hook: In a yard this size, nothing hides. A proposal should read the same way.
posts.caption:
A Pacific Beach lot gives you a few hundred square feet between the house and the fence, with neighbors on every side. Every inch gets used: a spa to sit in after a surf, a rinse shower by the door, a bench built into the fence line, a fire, and a patch of turf that never needs a mower.

We write our numbers the way we draw a yard like this. Every figure is backed by a walk of the property and a line by line scope, so you can see what each piece of the project is before anything starts. One firm, one plan, one honest number. Your project manager stays your one point of contact, and ten months after it’s finished we come back and walk it again.

By design, not by dispatch. References available on request.

The selections:
• Arterra porcelain pavers
• raised spa clad in matching porcelain
• cedar slat fence with a built in bench
• linear fire table with a Firegear burner
• SYNLawn turf · copper outdoor shower
